subject: Hearthline onboarding — identity & network runway (SSO/SCIM/IP/service accounts)
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@hearthline.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@hearthline.com>, security@hearthline.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Initial constraints for SSO/SCIM & network egress

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Security has a handful of non-negotiables we need to bake into the onboarding plan before we can open our firewall change window:

- Our environment only allows traffic to a set of static egress IPs (we need Redwood to provide a small set of fixed IPs for SSO/SCIM and webhook callbacks).
- SCIM provisioning must map our internal attribute orgUnit -> Redwood team/org attribute (we also need examples for group sync scope).
- Service accounts used for automation must be short-lived and rotate nightly; we cannot accept long-lived static keys.
- We will require SP-initiated SAML with an encrypted assertion and the following attributes in the assertion: email, sub, groups, and a customClaim:hr_org (we can share our full metadata).

Can you send a mutual action plan (MAP) with the timeline for: SAML metadata exchange, SCIM attribute mapping signoff, firewall exceptions, and a pre-prod cutover date? Also please attach sample SCIM mapping file and your preferred SAML metadata format.

Attached: our security checklist (summary) — sending to your CS and security contacts on copy.

Best,
Alice
Director of IT Integrations
Hearthline Health

[attachment: Hearthline_Security_Checklist.pdf]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@hearthline.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial constraints for SSO/SCIM & network egress

Alice — thanks for the clear list. We can accommodate the constraints but want to confirm a few details so the MAP is actionable. Draft MAP attached (MAP_Hearthline_Week1.xlsx) — highlights below and requested inputs in bold.

Proposed high-level run:
- Day 0 (metadata exchange): exchange SAML metadata (we support XML and URL endpoints). Please confirm if you prefer signed-encrypted metadata XML or meta endpoint.
- Day 1–2 (SCIM mapping): our SCIM integrator will provide a csv example for group scoping and attribute mapping; we need your canonical attribute names (orgUnit or department).
- Day 3 (network): we will provide 3 egress IPs for pre-prod and 3 for prod. Please confirm whether the firewall team needs CIDR ranges or single IPs.
- Day 4 (service accounts): we recommend provisioning a dedicated service identity with short-lived tokens (we provide a rotation script for your ops) and a scoped role for provisioning only.
- Day 5 (dry-run): run sync in pre-prod, monitor audit logs, and validate role mappings.

Key asks for your team (please reply inline):
1) SAML metadata format preference (XML file / metadata URL) — **Alice**
2) SCIM canonical attribute names + example users in a csv — **Samir**
3) Firewall change window target dates (preferred weekend window) — **Hearthline Security**

I've looped in Monica (Customer Success) and Ben (Security Engineering) and Priyom (Solutions) to help with the technical attachments and to own the pre-prod dry-run.

Attachments included: MAP_Hearthline_Week1.xlsx, request template for firewall.

Thanks — I'll schedule a 30-minute sync once we have the metadata.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Initial constraints for SSO/SCIM & network egress

Adding technical details from the eng side — copying the MAP rows into the thread so they’re visible: 

SAML / assertion recommendations:
- SP-initiated is fine; we can also support IdP-initiated but prefer SP-initiated for our flows.
- We can consume signed metadata XML or metadata URL. If you share signed XML we will validate with your cert.
- Encrypted assertions: support AES256 encryption; we will provide a public key for encryption.
- Assertion attributes we need: email (NameID or attribute), sub (stable id), groups (array), hr_org (custom claim). Group membership used for RBAC mapping.

SCIM notes:
- Our SCIM implementation supports users and groups v2, with attribute mapping customizable. Recommend providing a sample of 10 users (csv) with: externalId,email,userName,active,groups,orgUnit.
- For group sync scoping, we support whitelist of group names or a group-filter expression.

IP allowlist / egress:
- We can commit to two pairs of static NAT IPs for pre-prod and two pairs for prod (four IPs total per environment). We will provide CIDR /32 single-IP entries.
- If Hearthline requires regional egress, confirm the cloud region (we have us-west-2 and us-east-1 available).

Service accounts & tokens:
- We cannot issue customer-side long-lived API keys. Instead we will create a service identity in our IAM with a short-lived token exchange (currently 12-hour TTL, configurable down to 1 hour). We will share a rotation script and recommend a cron for nightly rotate.
- For automation that needs outbound webhooks from Hearthline to Redwood, use a per-environment callback secret rotated weekly.

Pre-prod cutover window suggestion: Nov 20–21 (Saturday night maintenance) — that gives time for metadata exchange and firewall ticket.

I’ll attach a sample SCIM mapping csv (SCIM_attribute_map_example.csv) and a SAML metadata template.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

[attachment: SCIM_attribute_map_example.csv]
[attachment: Redwood_SAML_Metadata_Template.xml]

Thanks Ben — that looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 
- We will supply signed metadata XML (per your template) and expect to receive your public key for encrypted assertions.
- For IPs: our firewall team requires single /32 entries and requests a ticket number to correlate changes. I’ll open the ticket once we have the exact IPs.
- For SCIM: I’ll attach a 10-user sample csv by EOD and flag which groups should be synced (we only want the 3 clinical groups).

Proposed cutover: we can do Nov 20, start 22:00 PST. If Redwood can provide the prod IPs and the token rotation script by Nov 18, we’ll be able to approve the firewall window.

Also please add in the MAP a checkpoint for org policy verification — our compliance team needs to confirm that user deprovision triggers an entitlement removal within 10 minutes of SCIM deactivation.

Thanks — Samir
